data.gender_notes: Ranbir is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ranbir is a name derived from the Sanskrit words 'Ran' meaning 'Lord' and 'Bir' meaning 'warrior' or 'battle'. This name is often given to a baby boy in Hindu tradition to signify strength, courage, and leadership. The name Ranbir carries the meaning “Lord of the battle” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ranbir usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the battle and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Ranbir Singh, the sixth Sikh guru (1571-1606 AD). He was born as 'Jodh' or 'Jodhia' in the Lodhi Rajput clan of the Sivalik Hills. He was given the name 'Ranbir' ('brave prince') by his father, Raja Randhia of Bir, after he displayed his courage by killing a tiger as a child.

Ranbir Singh (1783-1857 AD), the Maharaja of Punjab. He was the eldest son of Ranjit Singh, the founder of the Sikh Empire. Ranbir Singh expanded the empire, improving infrastructure, and strengthening the military. His reign saw relative peace and prosperity in the region.
